question: Why does acceleration fall after the motor's base speed?
expected_answer: Above base speed, the theoretical motor curve holds power constant and torque falls as P/ω; available wheel force falls.

question: How does the app calculate road load on a flat road?
expected_answer: It adds rolling force m g Crr and aerodynamic drag 0.5 ρ CdA v².

question: Why can a higher CdA lower top speed?
expected_answer: A larger CdA raises drag quadratically with speed, so force balance occurs sooner.

question: Why does wheel inertia change the acceleration time?
expected_answer: It adds J/r² to inertial mass, reducing acceleration for the same net force.

question: Does wheel inertia change steady flat-road top speed in this model?
expected_answer: No. It changes the acceleration inertial term but not steady force balance.

question: How does a smaller wheel radius affect launch force?
expected_answer: For fixed wheel torque, force rises because F = T/r; it also raises motor RPM at a given road speed.

question: What force balance defines the app's estimated top speed?
expected_answer: The first speed where available wheel force falls to road-load force.

question: What does the app mean by maximum startable gradient?
expected_answer: The highest searched grade with any speed at which peak wheel force meets resistance. It is not a thermal or traction guarantee.

question: Why can more peak torque improve launch but not high-speed acceleration?
expected_answer: Peak torque raises the low-speed region; above base speed the fixed power limit sets torque.

question: Why may higher peak power improve high-speed acceleration?
expected_answer: Above base speed, more available shaft power yields more torque and wheel force at a given RPM.

question: Does the Acceleration view integrate distance versus time?
expected_answer: No. It plots speed versus time and calculates target time and final speed; distance is not integrated in this view.

question: Is the current top-speed estimate a measured vehicle road test?
expected_answer: No. It is a model estimate from the configured capability curve and road resistance.

question: How is the theoretical motor torque-speed envelope built?
expected_answer: Peak torque is flat up to P/T base speed, then torque is P/ω.

question: How is the continuous motor curve limited?
expected_answer: It is the smaller of peak torque divided by the peak-to-rated ratio and continuous power divided by ω.

question: What happens to the acceleration calculation when a motor torque-speed file is uploaded?
expected_answer: The uploaded RPM–torque curve replaces the theoretical envelope, with interpolation of torque at motor RPM.

question: What is the motor RPM at 60 km/h for this gearing and wheel radius?
expected_answer: Approximately 4547 rpm from wheel speed times the 8:1 ratio.

question: Does the Powertrain Sizing tab implement a motor maximum-RPM cutoff?
expected_answer: No explicit maximum-RPM input or cutoff is applied in this tab.

question: What is the purpose of peak-to-rated torque ratio?
expected_answer: It sets the continuous torque plateau as peak torque divided by that ratio.

question: Which motor data columns does the upload expect?
expected_answer: A motor speed and motor torque column; the app normalizes them as motor_speed and motor_torque.

question: How is a configured battery DC current cap applied to motor torque?
expected_answer: The shaft-power ceiling is voltage times DC current limit times motor/controller efficiency; torque is clipped at each RPM.

question: Which efficiency data does the battery cap use when maps are loaded?
expected_answer: It uses the motor and controller efficiency maps at the operating point; the constant fallback applies without maps.

question: Is the controller phase-current limit independently configured in Powertrain Sizing?
expected_answer: No. The tab has an optional battery DC current limit, not a separate controller phase-current limit.

question: Can the optional battery DC power cap affect the calculated top speed?
expected_answer: Yes, if it clips available shaft torque/power near the force crossing.

question: Is thermal derating of the controller simulated in the Acceleration plot?
expected_answer: No controller thermal derating curve is applied there.

question: Can the app establish whether this controller's phase current is safe from the shown inputs?
expected_answer: No. It needs phase-current and controller ratings/test evidence; the optional DC current field alone is insufficient.

question: If I raise the reduction ratio, what should happen to launch force and motor RPM at a fixed road speed?
expected_answer: Launch force and motor RPM both rise, until another cap changes the result.

question: Why might a higher reduction ratio improve gradeability but hurt high-speed performance?
expected_answer: It multiplies low-speed wheel torque but moves the motor farther along its falling-torque/high-RPM envelope at a given vehicle speed.

question: If I increase mass, which of acceleration and steady top speed are affected?
expected_answer: Acceleration worsens because inertial mass and rolling/grade load rise; flat-road top speed can also fall because rolling resistance rises.

question: If CdA falls while motor power stays fixed, which part of the run benefits most?
expected_answer: Higher speeds benefit most because aerodynamic drag grows with v².

question: Could raising peak torque leave 0–60 nearly unchanged if peak power remains fixed?
expected_answer: Yes. Raising peak torque moves base speed lower; power-limited portions of 0–60 may stay similar.

question: Why can an uploaded curve change both acceleration and top-speed estimates?
expected_answer: Both use available wheel force derived from the uploaded RPM–torque curve, compared with road load.

question: According to the motor-testing document, how is winding resistance measured?
expected_answer: Four-wire Kelvin measurement at controlled temperature, corrected to a reference temperature.

question: What does the testing document say to measure for a torque-speed curve?
expected_answer: A dynamometer sweep across speed and torque points under controlled temperature.

question: How is the motor efficiency map tested in the motor-testing document?
expected_answer: Grid testing over speed and torque, with motoring and regeneration if supported.

question: In the motor-testing document, which test confirms peak power and continuous power?
expected_answer: Rated thermal soak followed by peak-current or overload windows per specification.

question: What does the motor-testing document prescribe for temperature rise at rated duty?
expected_answer: Thermal soak on a dynamometer until steady state, measuring winding, magnet, bearing and housing temperatures.

question: What is measured in the motor-testing document's field-weakening or overspeed-region test?
expected_answer: Current, voltage and torque at high speed.

question: How should the testing plan validate controller over-current protection?
expected_answer: Controlled fault injection and measurement of protection reaction timing.

question: How does the motor-testing document say to check controller over-voltage and under-voltage behavior?
expected_answer: Voltage sweep and fault logging.

question: What are the hub-motor-specific test priorities in section 5.1?
expected_answer: IP, salt spray, mud splash, wheel-end shock, bearing endurance, tyre/rim interface and wheel balance.

question: What additional test emphasis does section 5.2 of the motor-testing document give a mid-mount motor?
expected_answer: Gearbox efficiency, lubricant ageing, backlash, coupling fatigue, controller packaging, ducting and frame vibration.

question: Which reference covers motor ingress protection in the testing document?

question: Which India reference in the motor-testing document addresses EMC for the motor controller and harness?

question: Which standard family listed in the motor-testing document covers rotating-machine ratings and performance?

question: What test detects rotor rub, bearing drag or winding anomalies at end of line?
expected_answer: A no-load current screen at fixed speed against limits.

question: What does the motor-testing document's recommended test-record schema require for inputs and measurements?
expected_answer: Inputs include voltage, current, speed, torque, temperature and load profile; measurements record what was observed.

question: Compare the motor-testing document's torque-speed and efficiency-map test setups.
expected_answer: Both use speed and torque points; the torque-speed curve is a dynamometer sweep, while the efficiency map is a grid with input/output power and possible regeneration.

question: Which mechanical and environmental tests are especially important for a hub motor?
expected_answer: Wheel hub durability and bearing endurance, plus ingress, salt-spray and mud exposure.
